- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, adjust forecast toward center of that range.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 forecast values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
